## Goal

Collapse `X-Local-Preference` to **two** live values and make the intended one the default:

1. retire the deprecated `local-only` wire value (**loud `400`**, never a silent demotion);
2. retire `prefer-local` and make **`remote-ok` the default**, where `remote-ok` means *"try local first, but never wait for it"*: the local route stays in the chain, and if it cannot serve the request **right now** the request steps straight to the next provider in the chain (no queueing, no deferral, no refusal);
3. give `local-preferred` a **bounded deferral**: once a session has been told to retry three times (three consecutive retryable local-capacity `429`s carrying `Retry-After`), the proxy stops refusing and lets the request fall back to a remote tier instead of handing the client a fourth retryable `429`.

discovered-from:LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (the item that introduced the `local-only` → `local-preferred` alias and left its removal milestone open as a non-blocking advisory question), LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY (the epic whose parent assumption A2 this item amends).

## Problem statement

Two contracts are wrong today.

1. **`local-only` is accepted indefinitely.** `admission_reserve.LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` still maps `local-only` → `local-preferred`, with a "one `WARNING` per request" deprecation line. The alias was shipped as a wire-compatibility bridge (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 AC1/AC5) and the open question of a removal milestone was never answered (`plan` session 2026-10-28, "OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking …)"). It has now outlived its purpose: the value carries no distinct meaning, and it hides which intent a deployed client actually asked for.
2. **`local-preferred` deferral is unbounded.** Parent assumption A2 of LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY states the proxy "never silently promotes the request to a paid provider" while the prompt still fits local. A client that retries forever therefore receives retryable `429`s forever: the 2026-10-25 incident (seven retries against `Retry-After: 1`, LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) is the same failure shape seen from the client side. An unattended worker whose pane polls a permanently contended local GPU gets no answer at all, only a chain of "retry later" responses — and no proxy-side bound exists on how long that can continue.

3. **The default value is `prefer-local`, and `remote-ok` means the opposite of its name.** `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_PREFER_LOCAL` (`admission_reserve.py:79`), so an absent header asks for local-first service — and today that default **queues** for up to `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60 s, `contention_queue_policy: queue`, `config.yaml:1756`) when the local slot is busy. Meanwhile `remote-ok` does not mean "remote is acceptable": `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:461`) **strips every local entry**, so a `remote-ok` client can never use the GPU at all. The operator's intended policy is a third thing, expressed with the second value: `remote-ok` = *try local, never wait for it* — and it is the **default**. No decision for this exists in the tree today (`wl search` for a `prefer-local` removal or a `remote-ok` default returns nothing; `proxy/docs/routing.md:1317`, `:1329` and `proxy/config.yaml:1925-1927` document the current behaviour), so this item records it as the first written decision.

The user-visible symptom of the first two is a **livelock**: `local-preferred` work that could be completed on a remote tier (at a cost) never completes, and never tells the operator that its deferral budget has been spent.

## Users

- **The operator running unattended local-first work** — *"As an operator, I want my `local-preferred` work to eventually complete even while the local GPU stays busy, so an overnight pane does not spin on retryable 429s until morning; and I want the remote spend to be visible in `proxy.log` and in the response headers, not silent."*
- **The client that pinned the old spelling** — *"As a client that still sends `local-only`, I want a loud, actionable failure telling me to send `local-preferred`, rather than being silently re-interpreted as a policy I did not ask for."*
- **The headerless client** (pi, an OpenAI SDK caller, `curl`, any tool that never sets the header) — *"As a headerless client, I want the GPU when it is free and a remote answer the instant it is not — never a 60 s wait in a queue I did not ask for, and never a silent demotion."*
- **The client that genuinely cannot tolerate remote spend** — *"As a cost-capped worker, I want a documented, config-level way to guarantee zero remote spend for my model, so that the new escalation on `local-preferred` cannot bill me."* (Served today by a chain with no remote entries — the `private` model — not by a preference value; see Assumption A4.)

## Acceptance Criteria

### Part A — retire the `local-only` wire value

- **AC1 (retirement is loud, never a silent demotion).** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` is no longer normalised to `local-preferred`. It is rejected with `400` and a stable JSON body (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only chain rather than a preference value), emitted **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written (fake transport records zero upstream calls). It must **not** silently degrade to the `prefer-local` default: a silent demotion would let a cost-capped client be billed without consent — the exact 2026-10-25 defect (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG) — and would make the retirement unobservable.
- **AC2 (the rejection is observable and attributable).** Each rejection emits exactly one `WARNING` line carrying the retired value, the resolved successor guidance and the session id when present, so a deployed client still on the old spelling is identifiable from `proxy.log` alone.
- **AC3 (scope is the wire value only).** Only `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary changes. Explicitly unchanged: a provider *named* `local-only` (test fixtures in `proxy/test_home_page.py`, the `private` model notes), the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`, `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, `_log_local_only_refusal`), and the canonical reason token `local_only_no_local_route`. Rationale: renaming them is churn that breaks log-grep consumers for no behavioural gain — recorded as a scope decision, not an oversight.
- **AC4 (vocabulary tests and unknown-value observability).** `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"})` returns the retired/unparseable outcome (not the default); every still-valid value and the absent header keep their exact result; one test asserts the alias table no longer contains `local-only` so the removal cannot silently regress.
- **AC22 (an unknown value logs a `WARNING`, not `DEBUG`).** An unrecognised `X-Local-Preference` value still **resolves** to the default (`remote-ok`) — the header stays additive, no `400` — but the fallback is now logged at **`WARNING`**, naming the raw value received and the default it resolved to. Today that line is `DEBUG` (`admission_reserve.py:686-688`), so a client sending a typo (`local-preffered`, a stale `local_only` with an underscore, `local-only ` with stray whitespace that is not stripped into the alias path) silently loses its intent with nothing in `proxy.log`. The line is emitted **once per request** (the parsed value is cached on the request by `_request_local_preference()` / `priority.local_preference_for_request()`, so it is not one line per routing decision), includes the session id when resolvable, and never raises. Tests: one `caplog` row per sample typo asserting `WARNING` level + both the raw and resolved values, one row asserting a *valid* value logs nothing at `WARNING` from this path, and one row asserting the unknown value still routes as `remote-ok`.

### Part B — bounded deferral for `local-preferred`

- **AC5 (bounded retry budget).** A per-session counter of **consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals** is maintained. Retryable refusals 1, 2 and 3 behave exactly as today (honouring the reason-driven timing contract of LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X: `retryable: true`, `Retry-After` / `retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`). When the counter has reached **3**, the *next* request from that session is **not** refused again: the local entry is dropped from the chain for that request and the remote tiers serve it.
- **AC6 (promotion is visible, never silent).** An escalation-driven promotion returns the upstream status (normally `200`) with `X-Local-Route: remote` **and** a new canonical fallback reason token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` added to `admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` (so the response header, the body `reason` where a body exists, and the `reason=` log field cannot drift apart), plus exactly one log line naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold. An escalation promotion must be distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion (LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4) in both headers and logs.
- **AC7 (the refusal advertises its budget).** Every retryable refusal body gains `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third and last refusal), so a client can decide to compact or switch preference instead of discovering the escalation by surprise. Purely additive: every pre-existing field, header and key order is unchanged and an existing client that ignores unknown keys is unaffected.
- **AC8 (counter lifecycle and reset).** The counter resets when: the session is served locally (a successful local dispatch); a non-retryable refusal or a `too_large` promotion occurs; the entry exceeds its TTL; or `local_deferral_max_refusals` is reconfigured. The store is bounded (entry cap + TTL, no unbounded growth across sessions) and is keyed per session id — a request without a resolvable session id keeps today's behaviour (refuse; there is no stable key to count against), asserted by a test.
- **AC9 (unchanged intents).** `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` are byte-identical to today on every path, asserted by the existing matrix rows unmodified. `local-preferred` is now the **only** pin-local value, so the escalation applies to every pinned request; the cost-capped escape hatch is a chain with no remote entries (Assumption A4), asserted by a test row showing a remote-less chain keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating.
- **AC10 (one knob, defaulted on).** The threshold is the single new config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`; `0` disables the escalation, restoring today's unbounded deferral), documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing "server restart required" convention. No other default changes and no second threshold source.

### Part C — retire `prefer-local`; make `remote-ok` the default

- **AC14 (`prefer-local` retired, loudly).** `prefer-local` leaves `VALID_PREFERENCES`. An **explicit** `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` is rejected with the same stable shape as AC1 (`400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`) rather than being silently resolved to the new default. Rationale is symmetric to AC1: an explicit `prefer-local` means "use local when it fits", while the new default `remote-ok` means "do not attempt local" — silently reinterpreting it would deliver the **opposite** of the client's request with no signal (a local-first client sent to a paid provider).
- **AC15 (`remote-ok` keeps the local route; it stops meaning "strip local").** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the **only** preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as `prefer-local` attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (`calls` include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces **no** `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC16 (no preference can empty a chain; remote-less models keep working).** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11218`, `:11915`). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC17 (the active default is observable).** Exactly one log line at startup (or on the first dispatch) names the active `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` and the retired values, so an operator can prove from `proxy.log` which vocabulary policy the *running* proxy applies — a deploy that ships the code without the intended config is otherwise invisible. Routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key (`preference=remote-ok` for headerless requests).
- **AC18 (the expected behaviour shift is documented, not later misread as a regression).** The item records the two shifts: (a) **no queue wait by default** — `contention_queue_dispatch` / `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` lines disappear for headerless traffic, so the measured `queued_duration` median drops to ~0 and the remote share rises whenever the GPU is busy at request time; (b) local serving is now **opportunistic** — a headerless request is served locally only when a slot is free at that instant, so local utilisation falls and `X-Local-Route: remote` with a fall-through reason becomes the common outcome under contention. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary); the expectation is stated in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and in the completion comment so the daily proxy-usage report's shift is not mistaken for a local-serving defect.
- **AC19 (test sweep).** Every test that relied on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly (16 modules reference `prefer-local`, ~55 occurrences outside `__pycache__`), and the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default so a silent revert fails.
- **AC20 (a `remote-ok` request never waits: immediate step to the next provider).** When the local route cannot dispatch **right now** — slot saturated (`cur_local >= max_local`), prefill-ETA over the wait budget, local cooldown, residency/`resident_prefix_insufficient`/thrash skip, lease held by another session, per-entry context cap — a `remote-ok` request falls through to the next chain entry **without queueing and without deferring**: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (`provider.py:7978-8016`) must not enqueue for this preference (it returns `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent behaviour), so no `contention_queue_*` wait is spent and no `429` is produced for local capacity. Assertions: with a saturated local gate the response's `X-Local-Route` is `remote`, the request's `contention_queue` wait is 0, and exactly one upstream call (the remote entry) is made — for each exit in the enumeration above, one row each. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics and is therefore unchanged.
- **AC21 (the default is `remote-ok`).** `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`, so an **absent header** and any genuinely unknown value resolve to `remote-ok` and inherit AC15 + AC20. `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)` — exactly two live values. The knock-on surface is stated for the reader, because it is now the *default* path rather than a niche value: the prefill-ETA admission guard still runs (it decides whether local can serve now) but its **refusal** outcome is unreachable for this preference, and the contention queue, the deferral/retry surface and `POST /llama/local/reserve` are reachable only for `local-preferred` clients.

### Part D — cross-cutting

- **AC11 (tests).** Table-driven coverage, each row asserting its own observable: retired-value `400` per entry point (with zero upstream calls and zero queue/lease writes); refusals 1–3 keep the timing contract and report correct `deferral_refusals` / `deferral_refusals_remaining`; the fourth attempt from the same session dispatches remotely exactly once with `X-Local-Route: remote` + `deferral_refusals_exhausted` + the log line; counter reset on local success, on TTL expiry and on `too_large`; no-session-id requests unchanged; `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` no-regression rows plus a remote-less-chain row (no escalation); a docs-contract test tying the documented values and token to the implementation.
- **AC12 (docs).** `proxy/docs/routing.md` is updated: the preference table (`:1317` `prefer-local` default row, `:1329` "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`"), the per-exit fallthrough notes (`:1446`, `:1575`, `:1679`, `:1691`) and the wire-compatibility paragraph (`local-only` "is still accepted and normalised", ~line 1321) and the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph (~line 1529) are replaced with the retirement and its `400`; the `local-preferred` section (~line 1333, which currently states the proxy "never silently promotes") gains the bounded-deferral contract with the exact fields, headers and escalation token a client must honour. `proxy/config.yaml` commentary naming the legacy alias (~line 1945) is updated. The documented rule "Unknown values (and an absent header) behave as `prefer-local`" (`routing.md:1329`) becomes "resolve to `remote-ok` and log a `WARNING` naming the value", so a client author can tell accepted spellings from typos. Code docstrings for `parse_preference`, `_local_preference_pins_local` and the refusal builders are updated to match.
- **AC13 (suite).** The changed-scope test gate is green before commit; the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-29)

AC15 deletes the preference strip; the capacity strip and its remote-less carve-out stay byte-identical.
- `proxy/provider.py:11218-11221` and `:11915-11918` — both dispatch cycles carry an `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … "providers": []` branch that exists only to make an empty `remote-ok` chain deliberate. It becomes dead once AC15 lands (AC16 removes or neutralises it).
- `proxy/provider.py:7978-8016` — `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()`: the queue entry point whose `"fallback_policy"` action is the model for AC20's no-wait behaviour (policy is `queue` by default, `config.yaml:1756`).
- `proxy/config.yaml:1756` — `contention_queue_policy: queue` (the reason today's default *waits* up to 60 s, which AC20 removes for `remote-ok`).
- `proxy/config.yaml:400-408` — the `private` model: a single `type: local` provider (`local-qwen3`), i.e. the remote-less chain AC16 protects.

- Tests relying on the implicit default: 16 modules mention `prefer-local` (~55 occurrences) — `test_admission_reserve.py`, `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_local_non_admission_retry_timing.py`, `test_local_only_exit_docs.py`, `test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`, `test_routing_preference_logging.py` (`:117` `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREFER_LOCAL`, `:1833` absent-header param), `test_capacity_signal_verification.py`, among others.
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` (vocabulary/alias-table assertions), `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (deferrable/too-large matrix; `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` at `:592`), `test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_local_non_admission_retry_timing.py`, `test_local_admission_retry_docs.py`, `test_local_only_exit_docs.py` (pins the docs exit table; slices routing.md between two `###` headings), `test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`, `test_routing_preference_logging.py`.

## Desired change

1. **Vocabulary retirement (Part A).** Delete the alias mapping and make the retired value a *loud* `400` at the single parse/validation site, with its successor named. Fail-closed on ambiguity rather than defaulting: the `prefer-local` fallback stays for genuinely unknown values (unchanged), but the retired value is a known-and-withdrawn one.
2. **Bounded deferral (Part B).** Add one bounded per-session counter of consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, incremented where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability. At the threshold, the existing promotion mechanism strips the local entry for that request and stamps the new `deferral_refusals_exhausted` token, so the escalation reuses `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape rather than adding a third promotion path.
3. **Default inversion (Part C).** Three surgical edits, no new routing machinery: (i) delete `strip_by_preference` from `apply_local_preference()` so `remote-ok` keeps the local entry (AC15) and drop the now-dead empty-chain branches in both dispatch cycles (AC16); (ii) make `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` decline to enqueue for `remote-ok` so the fall-through is immediate (AC20); (iii) set `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`, drop `prefer-local` from `VALID_PREFERENCES`, and sweep the tests (AC21/AC19).
4. **Observability (AC2/AC6/AC7).** One rejection line, one escalation line, and two additive body fields on the refusal — no new log prefixes, no second classification of a refusal.

## Constraints

- **One implementation of each decision.** Retryability comes from `_refusal_retry_timing()`; the refusal classification comes from `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()`; the reason token comes from `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`; the pin decision comes from `_local_preference_pins_local()`. No parallel tables.
- **Truthful timing (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X).** Refusals 1–3 must not gain a timer they did not have, and the escalation must not advertise one (`retryable: false` on the terminal path, or no `Retry-After`, whichever the contract requires once the escalation fires).
- **Never silent, never unattributed.** An escalation that spends remote budget must be visible in headers *and* in `proxy.log` with the session id — the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson.
- **Bounded memory.** The counter store is capped and TTL'd; no unbounded per-session growth, no per-request state that survives its TTL.
- **No queue/lease leak.** An escalated request must not first enqueue into the contention queue and then also dispatch remotely; the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted by the fake-transport test.
- **Repository boundary.** Client-side migration (herdr, the pi extension) lives in the ContextHub store and is **out of scope**; it is recorded as coordination, not edited here.
- **The default must be safe for every client that never reads it.** A headerless caller cannot be expected to know the policy, so the default must (a) never produce an empty chain (AC16), (b) never queue, defer or refuse for local capacity (AC20/AC21), and (c) never be silently re-interpreted from an explicit value (AC14).
- **`remote-ok` must not regress into a strip.** After AC15 the value's *name* is historic: it means "remote is an acceptable answer", not "remote only". The `apply_local_preference()` docstring, `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/config.yaml` commentary must say so explicitly, because the shipped meaning of the value is the opposite and a future reader will otherwise restore the strip.
- **Wire compatibility is deliberately broken, twice, loudly.** This is the point of Part A; it must be documented with the exact `400` shape and a migration note rather than left to client discovery.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`, `PREF_PREFER_LOCAL`, `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES`, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, `parse_preference()` (including the `:686-688` unknown-value log level), `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` (+ `deferral_refusals_exhausted`), module docstring vocabulary paragraph.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `local_preference_for_request()` (docstring/default) and `apply_local_preference()` (`:461` `strip_by_preference` deleted; `:470-474` capacity carve-out kept verbatim).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (Part C) — the dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK` empty-chain branches (`:11218`, `:11915`) and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (`:7978-8016`, AC20's no-wait behaviour).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_preference_pins_local()` and its five call sites, `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`deferral_refusals*` fields), `_refusal_retry_timing()` (retryability hook), `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()`, `_promote_too_large_local_request()` (reused shape), `_stamp_local_routing_outcome()` / `_log_local_only_refusal()` (escalation line).
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (or a small dedicated module) — the bounded, TTL'd per-session refusal counter.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_deferral_max_refusals` (new, default 3) and the legacy-alias commentary (`:1945`).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `:1318`, `:1321`, `:1333`, `:1414`, `:1529`.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`, `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_local_non_admission_retry_timing.py`, `test_local_admission_retry_docs.py`, `test_local_only_exit_docs.py`, `test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`, `test_routing_preference_logging.py` — plus one new counter/escalation test module.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16** — introduced `local-only` as a deprecated alias (AC1/AC5) and left its removal milestone as a non-blocking open question; this item executes that retirement.
- **LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY** — the epic whose parent assumption **A2** ("deferral only ever *delays* a fits-local request; promotion happens solely on the `too_large` verdict") this item deliberately amends. The epic's desired-semantics bullet 1 and its `local-preferred` docs section must be read as amended once this lands.
- **LP-0MVTF3I2S009UXM3** (`local-exclusive`, hard cost-ceiling pin) — **deleted 2026-10-29** by operator decision (option C) in favour of this item. Recorded so a future reader knows the hard-pin value was considered and deliberately dropped, not forgotten: the vocabulary therefore has no "never leave local" preference, and a zero-remote-spend requirement is met at the chain level (Assumption A4). LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG's producer decision (2026-10-29) that relied on that item is annotated accordingly.
- **LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X** — truthful retry timing; the escalation must not reintroduce a useless timer.
- **LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG** — "never silently billed" (completed); the AC1 fail-closed choice follows its lesson.
- **LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN** (open) — rewrites the refusal `detail` / `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` strings; rebase rather than both editing the same prose.
- **LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4** — `too_large` promotion (reused shape; must stay distinguishable, AC6).
- **LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM** — the single routing-outcome line (`pinned` / `promoted`); the escalation outcome extends that vocabulary, not a new line family.
- **Client side (ContextHub, out of scope):** epic WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0, herdr WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, pi extension WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB, retryable-429 handling WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1 (counting key):** the counter is keyed by the request's session id (`X-Session-ID`), because retries arrive as separate HTTP requests and the session is the only stable identifier the proxy already persists; a request without a session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. Alternative (client-supplied attempt counter header) is rejected: it makes the bound advisory and client-controlled.
- **Assumption A2 (threshold semantics):** `local_deferral_max_refusals: 3` means "after **three** retryable refusals, the *next* request from this session is promoted". The refusal that would be the fourth is therefore never emitted; the third refusal's body reports `deferral_refusals_remaining: 0` so the client can see the escalation coming.
- **Assumption A3 (retirement is a hard `400`, not a silent demotion):** recorded as a producer decision point. The chosen default follows LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG ("never silently billed"); the alternative — degrade to `prefer-local` with a deprecation warning — is explicitly rejected in AC1 but may be overridden by the producer without re-cutting the item.
- **Assumption A5 (operator-confirmed semantics for `remote-ok`).** Confirmed explicitly on 2026-10-29: "`remote-ok` should NOT strip the local route. It should still try the local route, but if it fails to go local it will immediately step to the next model in the chain." Encoded as AC15 (no preference strip) + AC20 (immediate step, no queue). The shipped meaning of the value (`priority.py:461`, "removes the local provider from the chain") is therefore **redefined**, and the docstring/docs must state the new meaning.
- **Assumption A6 (remote-less chains).** The capacity strip's existing carve-out (`priority.py:470-474`) is kept verbatim and no preference may empty a chain: an explicit `remote-ok` on a `private` model is served **locally** rather than answered with "no remote route exists". This is the only rule that cannot regress `private`, and it costs only the (unreachable-in-practice) case of a client demanding remote-only on a model that has no remote entry — overridable.
- **Assumption A7 (the queue bypass is deliberate, not implicit).** "Immediately step to the next model" is read literally: `remote-ok` does **not** enter the contention queue, so the 60 s wait that today's default performs (`contention_queue_policy: queue`) never happens for this preference. If the intent was a pure rename of `prefer-local` — keep the queue, only rename the value — then AC20 is dropped and AC15/AC21 still stand; that is a one-line change to this item, no re-cut.
- **Assumption A4 (no hard-pin value; the former `local-exclusive` item was deleted).** LP-0MVTF3I2S009UXM3
  (`local-exclusive`) was deleted on 2026-10-29 (operator decision, option C), so no preference value
  expresses "never spend remote budget". A zero-remote-spend requirement is met at the **chain** level —
  a model whose chain contains only local entries (e.g. `private`) can never promote, and the AC9 test row
  pins that. The alternative of re-adding a hard-pin value later is a new work item, not a revision of this one.
- **Risk R1 (deployed clients break).** Any herdr worker or pi extension still sending `local-only` will start receiving `400`s. Mitigation: the client items are named in Related work, the `400` body names both successors, and the log line is attributable by session; the operator may override A3 to a deprecation window if a client cannot be migrated first.
- **Risk R2 (unexpected remote spend).** `local-preferred` now spends remote budget after three refusals where it previously spent none. Mitigation: bounded at 3, default configurable (`0` disables), stamped `X-Local-Route: remote` + `deferral_refusals_exhausted`, logged once with the session, documented prominently; a chain with no remote entries (`private`) remains the escape hatch for cost-capped clients (Assumption A4, AC9).
- **Risk R3 (state correctness).** A stale counter could escalate a session that had since been served locally. Mitigation: reset on local success, TTL, and an explicit test per reset trigger (AC8).
- **Risk R4 (doc-contract tests).** `test_local_only_exit_docs.py` slices routing.md between two `###` headings and maps token → outcome with later rows overwriting earlier; a new escalation row placed inside that range could silently flip the pinned "promoting ⇔ `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE_REASONS`" assertion. Mitigation: place the escalation prose outside both pinned ranges (the same hazard LP-0MVTF3I2S009UXM3 records).
- **Risk R5 (the default stops waiting, so busy-GPU traffic costs money).** Under AC20 a headerless request that arrives while the GPU is busy goes remote **immediately** instead of waiting up to 60 s for a slot. Local utilisation therefore tracks "was a slot free at request time", not "would a slot free up shortly": every burst of concurrent local work now pays for remote dispatch for all but one request. That is the requested policy (an evening of queued panes becomes an evening of paid parses), and it is bounded and visible: AC18 documents the metric shift, AC17 proves the active default from `proxy.log`, and any client that genuinely wants to wait can send `local-preferred`. If the intent was instead a pure rename of `prefer-local` (keep the 60 s queue), say so — see Assumption A7.
- **Risk R6 (remote-less models).** Under the *shipped* `remote-ok` semantics this was the highest-severity hazard: every headerless request to the `private` model would be filtered to an empty chain and answered with chain exhaustion. AC15 removes the strip that caused it and AC16 deletes the two branches that existed to make the empty chain deliberate, so a `private` model serves locally under every preference; the remaining risk is a future value reintroducing a preference-based strip, which AC19's invariant test (`apply_local_preference` never empties a chain) guards.
- **Risk R7 (retired-value churn in clients).** Two values are withdrawn in one change (`local-only`, `prefer-local`), so a client that sends either gets a `400`. Mitigation: both `400` bodies name the live successors, each rejection is logged once with the session, and the client-side items are named in Related work. The operator may stagger the two retirements (Part A then Part C) if a client can only be migrated once.
- **Scope-creep guard:** client migration, a per-preference quota ledger, a second status code for retirement, and any redesign of the contention queue are out of scope — record as new items if they surface.

## Provenance

No prior decision was found in the worklog or the tree (`wl search` for a `prefer-local` removal / `remote-ok` default returns nothing; the docs and `config.yaml` state the current `prefer-local` default), so this item carries the decision and its rationale rather than citing one.

reading `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` can read

live-work derivation pairs with `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`

Redefine `remote-ok` to *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: it keeps the local route and never waits for a slot (parent AC15, AC16, AC20). This child lands **before** the default inversion so the suite stays green - today `remote-ok` is a non-default value, so changing its meaning breaks no headerless caller.

## Goal

Make the value that will become the default safe to be the default: it attempts local when a slot is free, and steps straight to the next provider in the chain when local cannot serve the request right now - no queue entry, no deferral, no local-capacity `429`.

## Scope

- `apply_local_preference()` loses `strip_by_preference`; the capacity strip (`CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`) and its remote-less carve-out are kept byte-identical, so no preference can empty a chain.
- Remove (or neutralise) both dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: ... "providers": []` branches in the two dispatch cycles.
- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` declines to enqueue for `remote-ok`, returning the `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent outcome so the caller falls through immediately.
- Docstrings for `apply_local_preference`, `local_preference_for_request` and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` state the new meaning and the historic-name warning.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: the preference-table row for `remote-ok` and the per-exit fall-through notes that describe the strip are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone (no preference-based strip exists any more).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (no preference strip: `remote-ok` keeps the local route, parent AC15).** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the only preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as a headerless request attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (the upstream calls include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces no `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC3 (no preference can empty a chain, parent AC16).** The `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` is served locally (200, zero remote calls); the `private` model + absent header is unchanged at this stage; a normal chain with local down serves from the next remote entry, and exhaustion only when nothing is left to try. The two dead empty-chain branches are gone (grep-asserted). **Restates parent AC16:** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11445`, `:12142` as of 2026-10-30). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC4 (immediate step, no queue, parent AC20).** For each local-exit cause enumerated in parent AC20 (slot saturated, prefill-ETA over budget, local cooldown, residency/thrash skip, lease held, per-entry context cap) a `remote-ok` request produces `X-Local-Route: remote`, a `contention_queue` wait of 0, and exactly one upstream call. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics.

Retire the deprecated `local-only` wire value with a **loud** `400` (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4): never a silent demotion to `local-preferred` and never a silent resolution to the default. This child also builds the retirement mechanism that the later `prefer-local` retirement reuses, so the two retirements share exactly one implementation.

## Goal

A client still sending `local-only` gets an attributable, actionable failure instead of a policy it did not ask for (silent demotion to a local-first default could bill a cost-capped client - the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson).

## Scope

- Remove the `local-only` entry from `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (and delete the alias table if nothing remains in it) and drop `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` from the live vocabulary.
- Extend the **single** parse/validation site (`admission_reserve.parse_preference()`) with a retired-value outcome carrying the retired value and its successor guidance; no second parser and no per-call-site comparison.
- Emit the `400` at the request entry point **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written; the body is stable (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only *chain*).
- Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection, carrying the retired value, the successor guidance and the session id when present.
- Scope guard (parent AC3): provider names, the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` reason token stay unchanged.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_preference_vocabulary_v2.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (loud rejection, parent AC1).** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` returns `400` with `code: local_preference_retired` and the successor guidance, emitted before routing: the fake transport records zero upstream calls, and no queue entry, lease or cooldown state is created. **Restates parent AC1:** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` is no longer normalised to `local-preferred`. It is rejected with `400` and a stable JSON body (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only chain rather than a preference value), emitted **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written (fake transport records zero upstream calls). It must **not** silently degrade to the active default (`remote-ok`, AC21): a silent demotion would let a cost-capped client be billed without consent — the exact 2026-10-25 defect (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG) — and would make the retirement unobservable.
- **AC2 (not silently demoted, parent AC1).** No code path maps `local-only` to `local-preferred` or to `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`; a test asserts the response is a rejection even when the local route is free and the request would otherwise succeed locally.
- **AC3 (attributable, parent AC2).** Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection naming the retired value, the successor and the session id when one is present; a test asserts a single line and its fields.
- **AC4 (vocabulary, parent AC4).** The alias table no longer contains `local-only` (asserted so the removal cannot silently regress); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep their exact pre-change parse results; an unknown value still falls back to the default. **Restates parent AC4:** `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"})` returns the retired outcome (a `local_preference_retired` rejection, never `local-preferred` and never the default); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep today's exact result; the absent header resolves to the new default `remote-ok` (AC21); one test asserts the alias table no longer contains `local-only` so the removal cannot silently regress.
- **AC5 (scope discipline, parent AC3).** Grep-asserted: the provider fixtures named `local-only`, the `local_only_refused` log prefix, the `_build_local_only_refusal*` builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` token are untouched. **Restates parent AC3:** Only `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary changes. Explicitly unchanged: a provider *named* `local-only` (test fixtures in `proxy/test_home_page.py`, the `private` model notes), the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`, `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, `_log_local_only_refusal`), and the canonical reason token `local_only_no_local_route`. Rationale: renaming them is churn that breaks log-grep consumers for no behavioural gain — recorded as a scope decision, not an oversight.
- **AC6 (documented, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` and the `config.yaml` commentary describe the retirement and the exact `400` shape with a migration note; the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph is removed.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the alias mapping and the live constant; keep `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` only as a retired-value registry entry naming its successors.
2. Add the retired outcome to `parse_preference()` and thread it through the request entry point (fail closed before dispatch).
3. Add the rejection warning and the stable body at the same place the other preference `400`s are built.
4. Update docs/config commentary and fill in the corresponding contract specs.

Bound `local-preferred` deferral at **three** consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, then let the request fall back to remote instead of emitting a fourth `429` (parent AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10). Reuses the existing retryability decision and the existing promotion shape - no third promotion path and no second classification.

## Goal

An unattended `local-preferred` worker currently spins on retryable `429`s for as long as the GPU stays contended (the 2026-10-25 incident shape). After three refusals it must get an answer from a paid tier, visibly, rather than nothing.

## Scope

- New bounded, TTL'd, per-session counter store (`proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py`, or an equivalent small dedicated module) keyed by the sanitised `X-Session-ID`; no unbounded growth, entry cap + TTL.
- Increment where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability; the counter never re-classifies a refusal.
- At the threshold, strip the local entry for that request using `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape and stamp `X-Local-Route: remote` + the new canonical token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` (registered in `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`).
- Additive refusal-body fields `deferral_refusals` and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third refusal), with every pre-existing field and header unchanged.
- Exactly one log line per escalation naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold.
- New config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`, `0` disables) documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing server-restart convention.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py` (new module for the bounded counter store)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_deferral_budget.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (bounded budget, parent AC5).** Refusals 1, 2 and 3 are unchanged in timing and shape (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`); the fourth request from the same session is **not** refused - the local entry is dropped for that request and the remote tier serves it.
- **AC2 (visible, never silent, parent AC6).** The escalation returns the upstream status with `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: deferral_refusals_exhausted`; exactly one log line names the session, count and threshold; the escalation is distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion in both header and log; no `Retry-After` is advertised on the terminal path.
- **AC3 (the refusal advertises its budget, parent AC7).** The body reports `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third), purely additive - pre-existing fields, headers and key order unchanged.
- **AC4 (lifecycle and bounded memory, parent AC8).** The counter resets on a successful local dispatch, on a non-retryable refusal or `too_large` promotion, on TTL expiry, and on `local_deferral_max_refusals` reconfiguration; the store is capped and TTL'd; a request with no resolvable session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. One test per reset trigger.
- **AC5 (one knob, parent AC10).** `local_deferral_max_refusals` is the only threshold source (default `3`); `0` restores unbounded deferral; documented as restart-required; no other default changes.
- **AC6 (no queue/lease leak, parent Constraints).** An escalated request never first enqueues and then dispatches remotely - the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted with the fake transport.
- **AC7 (cost-capped escape hatch, parent AC9).** A remote-less chain (`private`) keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating; the pin-local predicate and its five call sites agree on the escalation decision.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the counter store with TTL, cap and a reset API; unit-test it directly.
2. Hook the increment into the single retryability decision and the reset into the local-success / `too_large` / non-retryable paths.
3. Reuse the `too_large` promotion shape for the escalation and register the token in the single token table.
4. Add the two body fields in the single refusal builder and the escalation log line.
5. Add the config key and its commentary, then fill in the deferral-budget specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child. Independent of the vocabulary children (do not rebase its counter onto a preference comparison - use the existing pin predicate).

# Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported saturated

Close the last 12 `saturated`-without-live-work polls by making the proxy
annotate the slot it is still draining: every abandonment records a matchable
identity (or an endpoint-wide entry), so a draining slot reads
`abandoned_busy` and only genuinely live work reports `saturated`.

## Problem statement

The AC1 fix (`LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK`) took `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` from **247 polls
(2.12 %)** to **12 polls (0.11 %)** over a comparable 11 h night, but not to
zero. Every remaining violation is a *draining* slot: llama-server has been
told to stop (the upstream stream was closed) yet has not freed the slot, and
nothing annotates it — `local_abandoned_slots=0`, so the poll reads
`saturated` even though nothing the proxy is waiting for occupies the pool.

The gap is therefore an **annotation** gap, not a liveness gap: the proxy
knows it abandoned the work, but the status builder cannot tie that
abandonment to the slot the backend is still draining.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether
  the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a draining ghost
  misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker).
  `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a ghost-driven
  `saturated` causes avoidable paid fallback.
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`.
  Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is
  as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when the pool holds only work the proxy abandoned, I
  want `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` (not `saturated`) so I can tell "busy
  because of us" from "busy because of live work".
- As the routing policy, I want a draining slot to never look saturated, so a
  needless cloud fallback is not triggered by work nobody is waiting for.
- As an analyst, I want each draining-slot abandonment attributable to a slot
  or to its endpoint, so a re-measured residual can be explained rather than
  merely counted.

## Evidence (from the AC4 run, preserved)

Re-measurement `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`, night 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30
07:00, artifacts in `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`
(`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, 12 rows, all fresh detail):

| episode | polls | attribution | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-30 06:57:36 | 3 (one second) | unattributable | `measured_cache_deficit` release 31 s earlier; `available_slots=0 total_slots=2 local_abandoned_slots=0`; pool idle again by 06:57:43 |
| 2026-10-30 06:01:20–21 | 2 | unattributable | — |
| 2026-10-29 20:19:25 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 295 s |
| 2026-10-29 20:35:03 | 1 | `prefill_deadline` | 14 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:36:23 | 2 | `no_progress_watchdog` | 182 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:47:30–31 | 2 | `prefill_deadline` | 48 s |
| 2026-10-30 01:43:11 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 520 s |

Two shapes of the same gap:

1. **Attributable (7 polls)** — an abandonment whose cancel succeeded leaves a
   slot that is still `is_processing` but carries **no** abandoned-registry
   entry (`local_abandoned_slots=0`), so the annotation does not fire.
2. **Unattributable (5 polls)** — a release with no slot identity at all
   (`measured_cache_deficit` on a record without a pinned slot), so the poll
   cannot be attributed even with the 600 s lookback.

Two further observations to confirm during implementation (not yet claimed as
causes):

- two rows (06:01:20, 01:43:11) report `available_slots=1` **alongside**
  `saturated`, which a purely-occupied pool cannot produce;
- one row reports `latency_ms=3355`, above the `/slots` detail budget, while
  `slots_detail_stale=false`.

If either turns out to be a distinct (non-lag) defect, record it as a
`discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` item rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it
   gave up on, or records an explicit "unknown slot, endpoint-wide" entry that
   the status builder can match to a processing slot on that endpoint (so a
   release without a slot id is still annotatable).
2. A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`
   until llama-server reports it free (registry TTL keeps it bounded; no
   leaked marker, no double decrement, no phantom lease).
3. `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`
   and never `idle`; a genuinely live, proxy-owned slot still reports
   `saturated` (the truthful-status contract of `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` is not
   weakened).
4. Deterministic tests (mocked `/slots` snapshot, injected clock) cover both
   shapes above, including the case where the draining slot is visible in a
   *fresh* snapshot, the endpoint-wide (unknown-slot) match, and the negative
   case (endpoint-wide entry present but the slot is owned by a live dispatch
   record → still `saturated`).
5. Re-measurement over a comparable night shows **0** `saturated`-without-live-
   work polls (baseline for this residual: 12 polls / 0.11 %, of which 5
   unattributable).
6. Full suite green through the `test` skill; docs updated where the
   abandonment → capacity interaction is described
   (`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Truthful status is not weakened** (`LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM`): an endpoint-wide
  match must never annotate a slot that a live dispatch record owns, and a
  fresh snapshot with genuinely live decode work must keep reporting
  `saturated`.
- The registry stays **in-process**, keyed by `(endpoint, slot)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s default), no
  timer task, no unbounded growth. An endpoint-wide entry needs a key that
  cannot collide with a real slot id.
- The annotation is **read-only status decoration**: it must never free or
  acquire capacity, double-decrement counters, or create a phantom lease.
- The status schema stays **additive** (`status_schema_version` 4:
  `abandoned*`, `local_abandoned_slots`, `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy`).
- **Measurement must remain possible.** `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  `_ABANDON_REASONS` currently excludes `measured_cache_deficit`, so that
  release is reported unattributable no matter how well the proxy annotates
  it — the set must be extended (with a test) or AC5 is unmeasurable.
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Existing state

- Registry: `_abandoned_slots` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), keyed
  `(endpoint_or_empty, slot_id)`; `_record_abandoned_slot` returns `None` when
  the slot id is not an `int`, so an unknown-slot abandonment is silently
  dropped — this is exactly the shape-2 gap.
- Matching: `_abandoned_slot_for(slot_id, endpoint=…)` tries the exact
  endpoint, then the legacy/default endpoint, then any endpoint carrying that
  slot id. There is no endpoint-wide (slot-less) match.
- Recording paths: `_release_unserved_dispatch` resolves the slot via
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup` *before* freeing the assignment (prefill deadline,
  client disconnect); session eviction resolves one slot per released record
  in `proxy/proxy/server.py`; the watchdog and orphan sweep record too.
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` passes **neither** slot id nor
  stream, which is the shape-2 source.
- Status builder: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` annotates `abandoned`,
  `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_at_seconds_ago`
  when the registry matches the slot id; `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0
  returns `abandoned_busy` when every generating slot is abandoned and keeps
  `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
- Residual behaviour: the 7 attributable polls reported
  `local_abandoned_slots=0` while a slot was `is_processing`, so the recorded
  identity did not match the draining slot (stale/mis-resolved id, or a slot
  the backend reassigned after the free) and the annotation never fired.
- Docs already describe the mechanism in
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (§ *Abandoned work*) and
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ *Abandoned local dispatches*).

## Desired change

1. Every abandonment path records either the slot it gave up on (resolved
   before the assignment is freed, and re-verified against the slot the
   backend actually reports) or an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry.
2. The status builder matches an endpoint-wide entry only to a processing slot
   on that endpoint that no live dispatch record owns, so the draining ghost is
   annotated and live work is not.
3. The annotation survives until llama-server reports the slot free (or the TTL
   elapses), and is dropped when the slot is observed free; re-abandoning
   refreshes it; no duplicate entries, no leak.
4. `capacity_hint` for a pool whose only work is draining stays
   `abandoned_busy` — never `saturated`, never `idle`.
5. `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` counts a `measured_cache_deficit`
   release as an abandonment event for attribution, with a test.
6. Docs updated where the abandonment → capacity interaction is described.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — abandoned-slot registry, release paths,
  endpoint-wide entry, slot re-verification.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status slot builder, endpoint-wide match,
  `compute_capacity_hint` (rule 0 unchanged in intent).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload
  (`local_abandoned_slots`).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — session-eviction slot resolution (if the recorded
  identity needs re-verification).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — registry, annotation and
  capacity-hint tests for both shapes.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — status payload contract.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — attribution set.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 7 attributable residuals are identity/matching failures,
  not TTL expiry — the longest release→poll gap observed is 520 s against a
  900 s TTL. Verify by logging the recorded slot id against the processing slot
  id during implementation.
- **Assumption:** AC5 (night re-measurement) is an operational run after
  deploy, mirroring the parent's child `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the plan step may
  decompose it into a follow-on child instead of blocking the code change.
- **Risk:** an endpoint-wide match annotates live work → weakens the truthful
  contract. Mitigation: require no live dispatch record for that slot, and
  cover the negative case with a deterministic test (AC4).
- **Risk:** a slot reported free and immediately reassigned could inherit a
  stale endpoint-wide entry. Mitigation: clear the entry on an observed free
  slot and keep the bounded TTL.
- **Risk (scope creep):** cooldown behaviour (`prefill_thrash_cooldown`) and
  the two anomalous rows (`available_slots=1`, 3.3 s latency) are **out of
  scope** here; record them as `discovered-from` items if confirmed.
- **Risk:** extending `_ABANDON_REASONS` changes the historical baseline
  (247 / 12 poll counts were computed with the narrower set). Mitigation: state
  the change in the report note and in the docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB` — parent: abandoned local dispatches leave
  llama-server busy (completed).
- `LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK` — AC1: abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel
  (completed; this item closes its residual).
- `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037` — AC4: re-measure one comparable night (completed;
  produced the 12-poll baseline).
- `LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2` — regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported
  saturated (completed).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — truthful-status contract (stale capacity hint
  reconciliation) that this item must not weaken.
- `LP-0MVT2KWF0000QTSM` — docs for abandoned-work status and cooldown scope
  (completed).
- Docs: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`,
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`; artifacts under
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is a producer interview needed before drafting, or does the seed context
  suffice?" — Answer (agent, from repo/worklog evidence): the seed context
  states the problem, the measured evidence, the target outcome, six testable
  ACs and the key files; no producer input is required to draft. Source:
  `wl show LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` (description authored by Map), evidence CSV in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent): the parent split re-measurement into its own child
  (`LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`), so the plan step should decompose AC5 the same way.
  **Open to producer override**, not blocking; recorded as an assumption above.
- Q: "Is `measured_cache_deficit` outside the abandonment reasons the
  verification script attributes?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes —
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` `_ABANDON_REASONS` lists only
  `prefill_deadline`, `session_evicted`, `no_progress_watchdog`,
  `client_disconnect`, while `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` exports
  `MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON`. Captured as constraint 5 / AC-relevant scope.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`?" — Answer (OPEN QUESTION, for implementation):
  not determinable from the artifacts alone (no recorded-slot-id field in the
  12-row CSV). Recorded as an assumption to verify with logging, not resolved
  at intake.
### Plan-stage Q&A (added by /skill:plan, session herdr-1793358530-3252013-3553)

- Q: "Is an endpoint-wide (slot-less) registry entry safe, or does it risk
  annotating live work and weakening the truthful contract?" — Answer (agent,
  code evidence + design): safe when the matcher requires that the processing
  slot has **no** lease owner and no live dispatch record; the negative case is
  pinned by a deterministic test before implementation
  (`LP-0MVUVHA55009EU4B`), and `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0 is unchanged in
  intent (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`). Source: `annotate_slots_for_status`
  already computes `owner_session_id`; `_build_slot_to_session_map` provides the
  dispatch-record binding.
- Q: "Should an endpoint-wide entry annotate a slot read from a *stale*
  `/slots` snapshot, and should a stale snapshot clear the entry?" — Answer
  (agent, design decision): annotate yes, clear **no**. The registry entry is
  fresh evidence about an abandonment, while `is_processing=false` is only
  trustworthy from a fresh snapshot; clearing on stale detail would let a
  cached "free" reading drop a live annotation, and the stale path is already
  reconciled by `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- Q: "Which key can represent 'endpoint-wide' without colliding with a real
  slot id?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): an `int` sentinel (`-1`) —
  llama-server slot ids in `/slots` and in `session._slot_owners` are
  non-negative, and the registry dict is typed `tuple[str, int]`, so a string
  sentinel would break the type contract. Recorded as a module constant so the

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the `local_lease_active` re-queue path to
honour the request's priority and to charge a request's queue budget **once per
turn**, so a `high`-priority request is never parked there and a request that
already waited cannot be handed a fresh 60 s.

## Defects found by code reading (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

`proxy/proxy/provider.py` has two `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites:

1. the `local_concurrency_limit` check — passes `priority=_priority`;
2. the `local_lease_active` retry (entered after the local dispatch returned a
   `local_lease_active` 503) — passes **no `priority=`**, so `priority=None`
   reaches both `_contention_queue_enabled(config, priority)` and
   `_prefill_admission_guard(..., priority=priority)`. The documented contract
   is that `high` priority **never queues**; on this path that contract is not
   enforced, and the guard pricing no longer knows the priority either.

Second defect: the lease-active path re-enters the queue **after** the request
already spent its wait (or none) at the concurrency gate, and nothing carries
the spend forward — `_contention_queue_remaining_seconds` is computed for the
*response* but the *next* `wait_for_local_slot` is called with the full
`max_wait_seconds`. A request can therefore accumulate up to two full budgets
in one turn, which inflates both the abandoned-wait denominator and the user's
latency (measured: 368 lease-active waits vs 143 dispatches in the post-change
24 h window, 61.1 % abandoned).

## Scope (bug fix, test-first)

- Pass the priority through on the lease-active call site.
- Carry the spent queue wait on the request and bound the second wait by the
  measured remainder, so cumulative queue wait never exceeds
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` for one turn.
- Keep the guardrails: no new knob, no change to the 60 s / 120 s values.

## Minimal implementation

- `provider.py`: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot(..., priority=_priority)` at the
  lease-active site; read/write the spent-wait marker through the existing
  `_set_queue_wait_on_request` / request attribute used by the deferral path,
  and pass `max_wait_seconds = min(cq_max, remainder)` (a keyword or a new
  helper argument on `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, defaulting to today's
  behaviour for callers that pass nothing).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`: optionally accept an already-spent
  duration so the waiter's own bookkeeping/`queued_duration` reflects the
  cumulative wait (no change to wake-up logic).
- Tests first: high-priority lease-active request does not queue
  (`fallback_policy`-equivalent, no `contention_queue_wait`); a request with a
  spent wait gets at most the remainder; an untouched path behaves
  byte-for-byte as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `local_lease_active` retry call site passes the request's priority, and a unit test asserts a `high`-priority request never waits in that queue (returns without a queue wait, matching the documented `high` never-queues contract).
- AC2: A request that already spent queue wait in the same turn is bounded by the measured remainder at the second wait, and a unit test asserts cumulative queue wait ≤ `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (no second full budget).
- AC3: `queued_duration` / the logged wait for the lease-active path reflects the cumulative wait for the turn (observable), and the `trigger=`/`cause=` fields from the observability sibling are populated on this path.
- AC4: Guardrails unchanged and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering test `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green; no new configuration knob.
- AC5: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing queue, deferral, reservation and lease tests pass unchanged in intent (any intent-preserving update is called out in the commit message).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py` (or the closest existing lease/queue suites)

## Related

- `LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C` — the completed item that made the lease denial queue.
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (holder-side capping) — NOT in scope here.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard (or the queue
admit criterion) to price the blocker class the diagnosis proves is holding the
slot — so a queue wait that cannot be served inside the 60 s budget is refused
up-front instead of burning the full budget and detouring remote — or, if the
diagnosis does not support a change, a committed decision that says so.

This is the behaviour-change slice. It is deliberately gated on the diagnosis
record so the change is driven by evidence, not by the assumption that the
guard is "too permissive".

## Context (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Measured in the post-change 24 h window: 314/517 enqueued waits abandoned, all
at the full budget; 225/314 were `reason=local_lease_active`; for the 176
abandonments with a session-level preceding guard decision, 170 were `admit`
with median `projected_wait_s = 35.8 s`. The guard's occupancy term prices peer

## Scope

- Extend the projected-wait quantity so the diagnosed blocker class is priced

  queues.

  caller plumbing in `provider.py`/`router_helpers.py` if the blocker snapshot
  is not already available) and the log fields that make the new term
